text:
Camila Reyes: Hey all — quick alignment needed on messaging + proof points for the Standard Demo v1 deck. Specifically the benchmark-y slides (latency/cost) + any “reliability” claims. Before we circulate to field, I need: (1) citations/source-of-truth links, (2) wording that’s defensible, (3) what we can say live vs what stays internal. Can you drop what you’re using + what you want approved?

Soojin Lee: Yep. In the current deck draft I have:
- “Predictable latency + lower unit cost via batching/caching”
- “Graceful fallback keeps apps online when capacity/model is constrained”
- “Token-level observability + cost breakdown in Console”

Soojin Lee: The part I need help on is the proof points slide. Right now it’s written as ranges (no hard numbers), but I still want a citation line + the conditions (model, hw, prompt length). I’m referencing the “Benchmark Proof Points - Slides Inputs” sheet but it’s not fully filled in.

Renee Sullivan: +1. For the talk track, AEs keep asking “how fast is it” and we need a consistent answer that doesn’t turn into a benchmark debate on the call. I’ve been saying: “we’ll share workload-specific numbers in eval; during demo we’ll show the levers + live telemetry.” But it would help to have 1–2 safe sentences.

Markus Klein: From SE perspective: please keep anything numeric as “typical range” and always tie to *workload + model + region*. Also we need a clear “if asked” line: we run customer-specific benchmark scripts in eval; the demo tenant is optimized but not a perfect replica.

Camila Reyes: Exactly. I’m fine with ranges but we still need to answer “based on what?”.

Camila Reyes: Soojin — can you link the deck section + the sheet tab you’re pulling from?

Soojin Lee: Drive links:
- Deck working draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/redwood-standard-demo-working (slides 9–12 are the proof points)
- Proof points sheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/benchmark-proof-points (tab “Public-safe ranges”)

Soojin Lee: The current footnote says “Internal benchmarks, Redwood Inference, 2024” which is probably too hand-wavy.

Logan Wright: Jumping in. For latency/cost ranges, we can cite the internal benchmark run IDs + dashboard snapshots, but we should standardize the caveats:
- HW: H100 SXM (hosted) and A100 80GB (dedicated pool)
- Model: “Redwood-verified Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct” (pinned version)
- Workload: chat completion, streaming on, ~1–2k input tokens, ~200 output tokens
- Concurrency: 16–64 depending on run

Logan Wright: I can export a “benchmark summary” PDF with run metadata + links to the internal Grafana panels. But we should not paste Grafana URLs into the deck.

Allison Grant: +1 on not embedding Grafana links in the deck. Recommend:
- Deck footnote: “Internal Redwood benchmarks (methodology available upon request)”
- Internal appendix (Confluence) contains: run IDs, raw charts, methodology, hardware, token distribution, and a “don’t compare apples to oranges” note.

Nikhil Sharma: On wording: avoid “fastest” / “best” / “guaranteed” unless it’s an SLA. For demo we can say:
- “optimized for low tail latency”
- “cost controls to reduce per-token spend”
- “fallback policies to maintain availability”

Nikhil Sharma: For reliability: we should say “policy-based fallback” and show it in Console, but not claim “zero downtime” or “always available.”

Camila Reyes: Great. What about the exact claim on slide 10? I saw “30–50% lower cost vs other inference providers” in one comment thread. That cannot ship.

Soojin Lee: Agree — that was a placeholder someone added during review. I already removed vendor comparisons from the latest draft. Current version is: “Meaningful cost reductions via batching + caching + quantization profiles (workload dependent).”

Soojin Lee: Can we approve that phrasing + add a footnote to methodology?

Markus Klein: Please also add “quality guardrails / evals” as the reason we don’t just crank quantization blindly. Prospects ask “what’s the quality hit?”

Renee Sullivan: +1. In talk track I want a crisp line: “We recommend cost levers with eval-backed guardrails; you can A/B and rollback.”

Jordan Blake: Looping in late — from CRO lens: we need proof points that create confidence but don’t trigger an audit. The goal of demo is: show levers + show telemetry + show deployment flexibility. If pressed on numbers: “we’ll run your workload during eval and share results.” Keep it consistent.

Camila Reyes: Thank you. Here’s what I need to close this out today:
1) Logan/Allison: a single internal doc we can reference as the “citation source” (not in deck) that contains run metadata.
2) Soojin: update slide footnotes to “Internal Redwood benchmarks; methodology available upon request” + list the high-level test conditions (HW class, model family, token ranges) without raw graphs.
3) Nikhil: quick pass on “safe verbs” (no absolutes) + reliability language.

Camila Reyes: Also: any public-facing compliance references? We should not imply SOC2/ISO status in the deck unless we have the standard approved language.

Allison Grant: On compliance wording: use the standard line from the Security FAQ (e.g., “security controls available; details under NDA / security package”). Don’t put badge icons on slides.

Nikhil Sharma: Re: reliability wording, suggest:
- Replace “guaranteed uptime via fallback” with “configurable fallback policies to reduce impact of capacity issues.”

Logan Wright: I can deliver an internal “Benchmark Summary v1” doc by EOD. It’ll include:
- run IDs
- date range
- configs
- token distributions
- p50/p95 latency and $/1M token *as internal reference only*

Logan Wright: But please don’t quote the $/1M token externally. Even as a range, it gets misused.

Camila Reyes: Understood. We’ll keep cost wording qualitative in deck; the live demo will show the cost dashboard, and we’ll offer to run their numbers in eval.

Soojin Lee: I’ll update slides now:
- remove any numeric cost claims
- add “workload dependent” to latency mentions
- add a callout box: “See it live: token-level latency + cost in Console”

Renee Sullivan: Can we also add a talk-track sidebar: “If asked for benchmarks: offer eval benchmark run + share methodology under NDA.”

Camila Reyes: Yes. Please paste the exact suggested phrasing here so I can approve once and we can reuse everywhere.

Renee Sullivan: Proposed talk track snippet:
“When teams ask about exact latency or unit cost, we’ll run your workload during evaluation and share results. In today’s demo we’ll show the specific controls—batching, caching, routing, and quantization profiles—and the Console telemetry so you can see how those levers affect cost and tail latency.”

Camila Reyes: Approved with one tweak: replace “we’ll” with “we can” (avoid sounding contractual). Also add “with your prompts/data” optionally.

Renee Sullivan: Updated:
“When teams ask about exact latency or unit cost, we can run your workload during evaluation (with your prompts/data) and share results. In today’s demo we’ll show the specific controls—batching, caching, routing, and quantization profiles—and the Console telemetry so you can see how those levers affect cost and tail latency.”

Camila Reyes: Perfect. :thumbsup:

Soojin Lee: I’ll roll these edits into the deck and tag you for final wording approval once the citations doc exists.

Allison Grant: I’ll create the internal Confluence page “Benchmark methodology + run registry (Demo v1)” and link it to the sheet + Logan’s summary.

Logan Wright: Ack. I’ll send the summary doc link in-thread when ready.

Camila Reyes: Thanks all. Once we have the internal citation page + updated slides, I’ll mark messaging “approved for field” and we can include it in the enablement email.

Camila Reyes: (Also please stop adding vendor names in comments lol — if you need competitive comparisons, keep it to the objection-handling doc, not the deck.)

Markus Klein: :100: noted.
